sentences.text: Mala @ Mala Kumari And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others

on 21 April, 2023
Author: Raj Beer Singh

Bench: Raj Beer Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 77
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 51932 of 2022
Applicant :- Mala @ Mala Kumari And Another
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Akhilesh Kumar Singh,Sandeep Kumar Maurya

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manvendra Dixit
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
The bail application of applicant no. 1 Mala @ Mala Kumari has already been dismissed as
withdrawn and now this bail application is confined only in respect of applicant no. 2 Pankaj Kumar.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in case crime No. 0509/2022, under Sections 363, 376, 120-B IPC & Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, police station Kotwali Deoria, District Deoria with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It was submitted that there are material contradictions in Mala @ Mala Kumari And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50419782/
1 the statements of victim, recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Mala @ Mala Kumari And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In her statement, recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., victim has not stated that applicant Pankaj Kumar has committed rape upon her.
As per ossification test, age of victim is 18 years and thus, she is a major girl and even as per alleged birth certificate, the age of victim was more than 17 years.

It was stated that at the time of alleged incident, applicant was present at his duty in the school, where he is working as driver and in this connection, a copy of duty-chart has been filed along with the supplementary affidavit.

Lastly,
it was submitted that the applicant is in judicial custody since 27.07.2022, having no criminal history, and that in case, applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail.

Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail and argued that victim has stated her age as 14 years and as per birth certificate, her age is less than 18 years and thus, she is a minor girl.
In her statement, recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., victim has stated that applicant Pankaj Kumar has committed rape upon her.
In view of attending facts and circumstances of the case, from the statement of victim, recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. also, it is apparent that victim was subjected to molestation.

After considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, gravity of the offence, severity of punishment and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, no case for grant of bail is made out.
Accordingly, the instant bail application filed on behalf of applicant Pankaj Kumar is rejected.

Order Date :- 21.4.2023 Anand  Mala @ Mala Kumari And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50419782/
